passage:
Last March my roommate Ojas met someone at a dance workshop, and by the next Saturday I barely recognised our flat. Our Sunday grocery run? Cancelled. The group trip to the waterfall? Ojas stayed back to wait for a call. Every dinner story was about Kiran: Kiran's poems, Kiran saying they were soulmates, Kiran wanting Ojas to move in by summer.
I'm Reena, and I'm bad at hard talks. I wrote three versions of what to say and deleted them all. In the end I just said, over chai, "I've noticed you've stopped doing the things that were yours. I might be wrong. I'm not going to lecture. I just miss you."
Ojas went quiet, then said I didn't understand real love. I said maybe not, and that the Sunday grocery run would still happen at ten.
Three Sundays later, Ojas showed up at ten, eyes puffy, holding the cloth bags.

qa.a: Ojas met Kiran at a dance workshop.

qa.q: Why did Reena delete three versions of what to say?
qa.a: Reena was nervous about hurting Ojas or sounding like a lecture, and admits to being bad at hard talks.

qa.q: Why was Reena's reply to "you don't understand real love" a wise choice?
qa.a: Reena did not argue or try to win; keeping the Sunday grocery run open at ten gave Ojas a way back without losing face.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Ojas to show up at ten, three Sundays later?
qa.a: Ojas likely felt hurt and embarrassed, but also relieved that the old plan was still there and that no one would say "I told you so".

Coach's note, college badminton team, Thursday.
Ira has missed four practices in ten days. She met someone at the start of the month, and since then she has stopped eating with the team, cancelled on her doubles partner, and talks only about him. Most of the team is annoyed.
Kamal, who has been her friend since school, handled it better than anyone. I overheard him at the gate today. He didn't lecture. He said, "Ira, I'm really glad you're happy. I just miss you. It's been ten days and it feels like you've disappeared. Is everything okay?"
Ira got defensive for a second. Kamal didn't push. "No pressure. I'm around. Saturday practice is at seven if you want."
I watched her face soften a little. She said she'd think about it.
I'll keep her place on the team open and check in with her myself next week.

qa.a: Ira has missed four practices in ten days.

qa.q: What was Kamal feeling when he spoke to Ira at the gate?
qa.a: Kamal felt worried and missed his friend, but he stayed gentle so she wouldn't feel judged.

qa.q: What did Kamal do that fits a wise response?
qa.a: He named what he noticed without shaming her, asked if everything was okay, and made clear he was still available.

qa.q: How might Ira feel after Kamal's words?
qa.a: Ira may feel defensive at first but also cared for, which is why her face softened a little.

Friday night
Mahima hasn't come to study group all week. Last Friday she met this guy at the metro café, and since then, it's all him. He picks her up. He texts her all through lectures. She cancelled her cousin's birthday. When I asked about the exam, she talked about how he said she's "the only real person he's ever met."
It's been one week.
I'm not jealous, I think. I'm worried. She seems so happy and also so far away. When I said I missed her, she said, "You'll understand when you find the one."
Tonight I texted her, carefully: "Hey, I'm really happy you're happy. I've just noticed you've dropped a lot of things this week, and I miss you. No judgement. I'm here if you ever want to talk. Chai on Sunday?"
She sent a heart. That's something.
Yusuf

passage: Every evening for two years, Jagdish and Pankaj had played cricket on the dry field behind the Hanuman temple in their village. This week Pankaj's spot at the crease stayed empty. On Thursday Jagdish found him outside the tea stall, phone glued to his ear. "Megha says we think exactly alike," Pankaj said when he hung up, eyes shining. "She wants me to call every hour. Bhai, it's only been a week and I already know." He had skipped his cousin's engagement, and the bus to exam coaching too. Jagdish felt the urge to say, "You've gone mad," and swallowed it. Instead he sat down on the bench. "You look happy. I've also noticed you've dropped cricket, coaching, everything, in one week. That's a lot, na?" Pankaj frowned, then shrugged. Jagdish stood up. "Match is at five tomorrow. Your bat's in my shed, whenever."
